narrative: OMX30 enters the session in a structural bull market (+2.8% above 200-MA) but technical conviction is severely compromised by sub-18 ADX reading (6.1) and position below the 50-day MA (-1.1%). Continental Europe broadly bid (DAX +0.49%, CAC +0.40%) and Asian recovery post-Hang Seng weakness provide modest tailwinds, but Brent crude's sharp 1.99% surge threatens to crimp both industrial input margins and consumer discretionary demand. The USD/SEK selloff (-0.24%) simultaneously weakens the export narrative that typically anchors Swedish equities. With RSI neutral at 51.3, MACD below signal, and Stochastic in no-man's-land (K=38.3, D=46.8), OMX30 lacks directional bias; the index sits only 3% from its 52-week high but trades at the lower edge of Bollinger bands—a setup favoring range-bound consolidation rather than breakout.
morningBrief: OMX30 opens on mixed signals: global equity tailwinds clash with technical hesitation and commodity headwinds. The ADX reading of 6.1 mandates a 30% confidence haircut on any tactical call; treat this as a low-conviction session. Industrials (28% weight) face margin pressure from Brent +1.99%, but the 85th percentile positioning and +2.8% bull-regime cushion should limit downside. Watch the 50-MA at ~3180 and lower Bollinger band support near 3085; a close below 3100 signals mean-reversion risk. Banks (18%) are net neutral—falling US 10Y yields (-0.37%) compress NIM expansion despite structural support. EUR/SEK weakness (-0.12%) and USD/SEK selling (-0.24%) argue for selective caution on large-cap exporters (Volvo, Atlas Copco, Ericsson). Oil price action is the session's primary tell; if Brent holds above 110, industrials stabilize; a break below 109 invites shorts. US Jobless Claims (14:30 CET) is the only calendar event; risk-off event could accelerate the correction already signaled by technical structure.
drivers: Modest global equity uptick (DAX +0.49%, Dow +1.02%) supports risk-on tone
Brent crude +1.99% pressures industrials and consumer spending despite global strength
Weak ADX (6.1) with bearish DI bias undermines conviction; OMX30 -1.1% below 50-MA signals correction risk
USD/SEK weakness (-0.24%) headwind for large exporters despite bull regime backdrop

sectorImpacts.reason: Brent crude +1.99% to 111 directly compresses input margins and raises near-term cost headwinds despite long-term inflation pass-through potential. ADX weakness limits upside even in bull regime.
US 10Y yield fell 37bp to 5.117%, reducing NIM expansion case. Swedish credit cycle stable, but flow headwind from falling global rates pressure net margin uplift. Structural support remains intact.
NASDAQ flat (-0.02%) and USD/SEK weakness (-0.24%) reduce export pricing power and sentiment tailwinds. No offsetting risk-off rotation into tech defensives given muted VIX rise.
Gold slightly negative (-0.14%), copper negative (-0.43%). No tailwind from commodities; industrial production concerns from oil spike may dampen volumes.
Brent crude surge (+1.99%) increases consumer transport/heating cost expectations, pressuring discretionary spending. EUR/SEK weakness (-0.12%) raises H&M sourcing costs.
Yield fall (-37bp) is nominally negative for refinancing, but Swedish property fundamentals stable. No major overhang today.

watchList.reason: Large industrial/export proxy; doubly exposed to Brent margin pressure and USD/SEK weakness. Break below 245 SEK (estimated support) targets 238 SEK.
Industrial bellwether; heavy exposure to input cost inflation from energy. Monitor for breakdown below 580 SEK near-term support.
Yield compression near-term pressure offset by sector stability and defensive valuation. Accumulate on dips if OMX30 holds above 3100.
Caught between USD/SEK headwind and muted tech sentiment. Range-bound 75–82 SEK until larger macro clarity emerges.
EUR/SEK weakness (-0.12%) + oil-driven consumer pressure = near-term headwind. Resistance at 195 SEK; support at 180 SEK critical.

econCalendarAlert: US Jobless Claims (14:30 CET) is sole event today. Swedish economic data silent. Risk: claims spike on renewed US labor softness → equity selloff, OMX30 tests 3085 support.
topRisk: ADX below 18 means trend confidence is critically low; any exogenous shock (hawkish Fed pivot, geopolitical event, earnings miss) could trigger fast, violent repricing. Oil remains catalyst for intraday volatility. Secondary risk: continued USD/SEK weakness erodes OMX30 export thesis despite global equity tailwinds.
technicalSummary: BUT: -1.1% below 50-MA and lower half of Bollinger bands signals correction risk, not confirmation.
MACD below signal (hist=-1.655) is early bearish divergence; RSI neutral (51.3) offers no mean-reversion clue yet.
ADX 6.1 = weak trend, bearish DI bias; reduce all confidence calls by 30% per rule. OMX30 is range-bound 3085–3180 until ADX crosses 18.
Stochastic K=46.8, D=38.3 (flat) = no directional edge. Expect chop.
ROC-90 +3.0% (neutral) confirms mid-cycle positioning without excitement.
